concerns.text: T004's verify step requires `code/utils/verify_pii_removal.py` to pass, and T009 re-runs it against the package, but NO task in T001–T010 creates or implements that script (plan.md's T-031b was dropped in consolidation). The verification is unexecutable as written — either add the script's implementation to a task or remove the dependency.

T008 asserts results match 'a reference stored in `data/reproducibility_ref.json`' but no task produces that reference file. An implementer cannot verify against a reference that nothing generates; T008 must specify how/when the reference is created (e.g., first run writes it, or a prior task records it).

T005 claims results conform to `analysis_result.schema.yaml`, but that contract's `test_type` enum allows only GLMM/LME (no McNemar) and its effect_size description covers Odds Ratio/Standardized Beta (no Cohen's d), both of which T005 is required to emit per FR-004/FR-005. The verification 'conforming to schema' is unexecutable for the accuracy rows and Cohen's d speed rows until the contract is fixed or T005 names a corrected contract.

T005 never reads or applies `data/interaction_logs/dropout_flags.json`, though the spec's dropout edge case requires excluding partial participants from paired analyses and T004 produces the flags. Add explicit handling (load dropout flags, exclude flagged participants, log count) so the edge case is executable.

T010 cites 'real-subject recruitment remains future work per `docs/scope_reduction.md`' but no task creates that document. Either add a task producing `docs/scope_reduction.md` or drop the reference; as written the implementer has no source for the claimed scope decision.

T003 bundles three deliverables (rule-based generator, GPU LLM runner with fallback, latency calibrator + main.py integration) plus two test files — too coarse for one task. Flag for atomization into separate tasks per artifact (generator, GPU runner, calibrator).
T004 bundles the simulator, Latin-square design, dropout handling, anonymization utility, and PII verification into one task — too coarse; atomize (e.g., design/simulation vs anonymization/PII).

Anonymization hashes IDs with a salt in `data/.salt` 'not committed', but T008's reproducibility test re-runs the analysis on a fresh runner — the salt (and thus hashed IDs) will not exist there. Specify how the salt is handled for reproducible reruns (e.g., committed dummy salt for simulated data, or salt-independent analysis grouping) so T008's verification is executable.
